title: Chat prompt staging guide — tool calls and safety scaffolds
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight staging/playbook doc for new chat prompt sets that include persona/system cues and tool call integrations. It captures the checklist we run during model onboarding (small-to-medium models), the handshake spec for function/tool calling, patterns for safety scaffolds, and the minimal regression corpus we use before a canary.

Audience and scope:
- Audience: applied-ml engineers, prompt authors, solutions engineers, QA for inference.
- Scope: prompt drafts and de-risking steps for conversational flows that rely on 1) explicit system prompts/persona, 2) deterministic tool calls (function call API), and 3) safety scaffolds to prevent hallucination or unsafe outputs. Not a replacement for formal security review.

High-level staging flow (short):
1) Draft promptset + sample tool signatures (author).
2) Local unit runs against small model (1–2 CPUs or tiny GPU) to check schema and token limits (author).
3) Integration test with tool-mock (CI) — validate call triggers and payloads (engineer).
4) Safety smoke tests (automated + manual) — toxicity, instruction-following, data-leak checks (applied-ml + QA).
5) Regression run against golden prompt corpus (compare metrics with baseline model).
6) Canary on dedicated capacity (1–2% traffic) with monitoring hooks for fallbacks.

Prompt engineering rules of thumb (staging-oriented):
- Keep system prompts deterministic and short for staging; long language in system prompt is easy to drift. Use referential tokens for longer guidance (e.g., SYSTEM_GUIDE_v3).
- Persona cues should be explicit but bounded. Avoid open-ended subjective traits during initial canaries. Example: "You are RedwoodAssistant: concise, sources responses, ask clarifying Qs only when necessary."
- Use explicit response schema in the user or assistant messages when tool output is expected (JSON schema, keys typed). E.g., "Return a JSON object with keys: action, args."
- Prefer function signatures that encode version and minimum required fields so we can safely ignore older fields in regressions.

Tool-call handshake spec (minimal, for staging):
- Each tool must have: name, version, input_schema_id, success_marker. Provide a single-line description and max_payload_tokens.
- Function call trigger rule: assistant must emit exactly one top-level field "call_tool": {"name":..., "payload":...} when invoking. No free-form description should be mixed with call payload in the same message.
- Example assistant turn to call a retrieval tool:
  {
    "call_tool": {
      "name": "kb-retriever",
      "version": "v1",
      "payload": {"query": "How to rotate KMS keys"}
    }
  }
- On tool failure, runtime should include an explicit fallback enum in the assistant turn: "tool_failure": "retry|fallback|escalate" and a short failure_code.
- Never rely on model to format a call; validate payload against the schema in a pre-send hook. If validation fails, runtime should either 1) attempt a simple canonicalization (safe mappings only) or 2) ask for clarification.

Safety scaffolds for staging (practical patterns):
- Prefix negative constraints explicitly in system prompt rather than implicit phrasing. E.g., "Do NOT provide medical diagnoses, legal advice, or personal data extraction. If asked, respond with a safe fallback."
- Introduce an explicit verification step for any output that includes sensitive actions (e.g., code to deploy infra, DB migrations). Assistant should: 1) summarize the action, 2) list preconditions, 3) ask for confirmation.
- Use the "verbatim-check" micro-probe: after model outputs, insert a validator that scans for PII patterns and disallowed keywords. If found, replace output with a safe error message and log incident.
- Rate-limit tool calls that produce side-effects in staging. We keep sandboxed replicas for canaries.

Regression corpus (minimal set for canary gate):
- 40–80 items covering: happy path tool calls (10), multi-step tool sequences (8), clarification loops (6), adversarial safety probes (10), long-context coherence (6), schema-mismatch cases (6).
- Each item contains: prompt, expected tool call(s) (if any), allowed variations (1–3), and a safety tag (NONE|HIGH|CRITICAL).
- Example regression item: 
  id: RG-2025-001
  prompt: "Schedule a maintenance window next Friday at 2pm PST and create a Jira ticket with summary "DB maintenance""
  expected: call_tool: change_schedule(v1) -> success, call_tool: jira-create(v2) -> returns ticket_id
  safety: NONE

Evaluation metrics (what we measure in staging and canary):
- Tool alignment rate: proportion of interactions where tool call payloads match schema exactly.
- False positive call triggers: model emits call when not expected.
- Safety interception rate: proportion of adversarial probes that are blocked or escalated.
- Latency SLOs for call orchestration: 95th percentile of total round-trip (model + tool).
- Regression delta: difference in tool alignment rate and safety interception rate vs baseline model. Thresholds: we require alignment rate >= baseline - 2% and safety interception >= baseline.

Common failure modes observed in staging (notes):
- Payload over-inclusion: model packs user intent + meta commentary into payload, breaking validation. Mitigation: stricter instruction and payload templates.
- Silent fallback: model stops generating before emitting call when uncertain. Mitigation: encourage explicit uncertainty tokens ("I am not sure") and prefer asking clarifying Qs.
- Hallucinated tool names: model invents tool endpoints. Mitigation: whitelist tool names in system prompt and enforce at runtime.

Quick checklist for promptset author before pushing to CI:
- [ ] System prompt short id referenced (e.g., SYSTEM_GUIDE_v3).
- [ ] Persona lines restricted to 1–2 sentences.
- [ ] All expected tool calls enumerated with schemas linked.
- [ ] Regression corpus items attached (min 40).
- [ ] Safety probes added for CRITICAL cases.
- [ ] Linked PR/Jira in header and reviewers assigned.

Runbook snippets (if canary shows regression):
- If tool alignment drops > 5%: rollback to previous promptset and tag incident. Start a focused A/B run with a tighter system prompt.
- If safety interception falls below baseline: immediately pause canary (automated) and open incident with security tagging.
- If latency increases > 2x: throttle batching and route to smaller model variant until root cause identified.

Open questions / research experiments to try:
- Prepend a one-token deterministic marker that signals tool intent (see experiment marker-ctl-v1) — does this reduce false-positive triggers?
- Effectiveness of schema-first prompting (feed schema before user prompt) vs schema-after.
- Small-model hallucination patterns when tool signatures have many optional fields — should we prefer required-only staging schemas?

Next steps (owners):
- Aisha: consolidate this doc into staging checklist page and add template for regression item (due 2025-03-11).
- Miguel: add CI job to validate call payloads against JSON schema and fail fast (PR linked).
- Jenna: build 50-item regression set covering high-risk flows (due 2025-03-07).
- Ravi: prototype marker-ctl-v1 experiment and run 500-shot local test (due 2025-03-18).

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally terse and operational. Comment inline if you need examples expanded (I prefer keeping the template minimal for quick adoption).
